Competencies

Show indicators at

Showing the L3 indicator for each competency. Open a competency to see all five levels.

  • Model interpretation5.2.1

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise that model behaviour can and should be inspected, not taken on trust.

    L2 Familiarity

    Run a SHAP/LIME / variable-importance analysis on a small pharma model following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Interpret a real pharma model with appropriate methods and explain it to stakeholders honestly.

    L4 Mastery

    Use interpretation to spot real problems (leakage, spurious features, subgroup failure) and act on them.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's interpretation practice for pharma ML.

  • Model assessment and sensitivity analysis5.2.2

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise that single point-estimates of performance hide a lot.

    L2 Familiarity

    Run a basic sensitivity check (e.g. swap a hyperparameter) on a pharma model following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Build assessment and sensitivity analysis into real pharma modelling: bootstrap, subgroup, design choices.

    L4 Mastery

    Stress-test pharma models systematically (data quirks, design choices, distribution shift) and report defensibly.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's assessment and sensitivity standards.

  • Importance of robust evaluation5.2.3

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise that evaluation choices can swing conclusions and that robust evaluation is non-negotiable in pharma.

    L2 Familiarity

    Apply a robust evaluation template (held-out, CV, calibration, subgroup) to a small pharma model.

    L3 Proficiency

    Design robust evaluation for a real pharma model and report it transparently.

    L4 Mastery

    Handle non-trivial evaluation contexts (external sites, prospective use, regulatory expectations) credibly.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's evaluation standards.

  • Challenges for machine learning5.2.4

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise common ML failure modes — overfitting, leakage, distribution shift, label noise, bias.

    L2 Familiarity

    Spot one of these failure modes in a pharma example following a checklist.

    L3 Proficiency

    Diagnose and mitigate these failure modes in real pharma models.

    L4 Mastery

    Anticipate failure modes from project design and instrument for them ahead of time.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's defensive ML practices for pharma.

  • Learning algorithms as principled optimization approaches5.2.5

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise that ML algorithms are usually solving an optimisation problem with assumptions and trade-offs.

    L2 Familiarity

    Read a loss function and explain what it is optimising on a pharma example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Choose and modify loss functions / regularisers appropriately for a real pharma problem.

    L4 Mastery

    Reason about optimisation behaviour in pharma ML (convergence, identifiability, conditioning) and act on it.

    L5 Expertise

    Contribute methods or set the team's principled-optimisation practice.

Pharma examples

Each example is tagged with the competency and level it shows. Tags open that level.

  • A SHAP analysis that reveals a model relying on a leaky proxy variableModel interpretation L4Challenges for machine learning L4
  • A sensitivity analysis varying preprocessing choices to test robustnessModel assessment and sensitivity analysis L4
  • A held-out external-site evaluation that decides whether to deployImportance of robust evaluation L4

Typical stack

explainability and interpretation tooling (shap, lime, iml, tidymodels parsnip + workflows); robust evaluation harnesses; uncertainty quantification (conformalInference, Bayesian tooling); optimisation theory awareness.
